skill.displayName: drivectl - your command-line tool for interacting with Google Drive

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for a CLI wrapper around Google Drive/Docs/Sheets, but it allows dynamic calls to arbitrary Google APIs and asks the user to provide local OAuth client secrets while having no provenance for the drivectl binary — this expands its effective scope and risk beyond what the short description implies.

dimensions.detail: The skill's declared purpose is Drive/Docs/Sheets via the drivectl CLI, and the instructions match that. However, the discovery/call functionality explicitly permits invoking almost any Google API (Calendar, Gmail, etc.), which is broader than the description implies.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to use a local OAuth client_secret.json and to authenticate (tokens cached locally). It also describes a 'drivectl call' mode that can dynamically execute arbitrary Google APIs. The skill therefore requires access to local credential files and can perform API calls outside Drive/Docs/Sheets scope — this increases the attack surface and privacy risk.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only). That reduces the disk-write and remote-code risk, but it means the user/agent must supply the drivectl binary themselves; the skill provides no provenance or safe install instructions for that binary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata lists no required env vars or credentials, but the runtime instructions require a local OAuth client_secret.json and user authorization. The lack of declared credentials is inconsistent with the fact that using the tool requires sensitive OAuth client credentials and cached tokens. The skill does not request unrelated system secrets, but it does rely on user-supplied credentials whose scope can be broad.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default but not, on its own, a red flag here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before using or installing this skill: 1) Verify and obtain drivectl from a trusted source and inspect its code/binary — the skill provides none. 2) Do not upload or hand over your OAuth client_secret.json to untrusted systems; prefer creating an OAuth client with minimum scopes needed and review granted scopes during auth. 3) Be aware the 'call' discovery feature can access other Google APIs (Calendar, Gmail, etc.); only authorize with the least-privilege scopes and consider running in an isolated environment. 4) If you need higher assurance, ask the skill author for provenance (homepage, repo) or request an install spec/checksum for drivectl before trusting it with your Google credentials.
